title: Quantization artifact lineage: hashing, provenance, rollback for FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Establish reproducible provenance and versioning for quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8 profiles, calibration params, per-layer scales) including content hashing, immutable metadata, and safe rollback semantics for serving.
acceptance_criteria: Every quantization artifact (profile + calibration dataset fingerprint + tool version) is uniquely identified by a content hash recorded in the artifact registry
Artifact metadata contains tool version, calibration seed/commit, dataset fingerprint, model commit hash, and quantization parameters and is queryable via Console and API
Serving runtime can atomically switch to a previous artifact using recorded provenance without manual file edits
Calibration/accuracy validation reports are linked to artifact entries and stored immutably
End-to-end reproducibility demonstrated in an internal eval with <=0.5% accuracy variance when re-running calibration using same inputs and tool version
proposed_solution: Create an artifact spec and registry. Compute a canonical content hash (SHA-256) over normalized JSON of: model_commit, quant_profile (per-layer int8/fp8 params), calibration-config (dataset fingerprint, random seeds, preprocessing), tool_version, build_info. Store artifact blob in S3-compatible store with path by hash and write immutable metadata entry to Postgres-backed artifact-registry service via API. Expose registry + APIs for lookup, compare, and rollback. Add client-side SDK helpers to compute canonical hashes during calibration. Integrate with Console to visualize lineage and validation reports.
artifact_schema: Fields: artifact_hash, artifact_type, model_commit_hash, quant_format (FP8|INT8), per_layer_params (serialized list), calibration_dataset_fingerprint, calibration_seed, tool_version, calibration_time_utc, validation_report_link, created_by, created_at. Hash computed over canonical utf8 JSON with sorted keys and normalized floats (6-decimal rounding).
implementation_tasks: Design canonicalization rules for quant_profile JSON and write unit tests
Implement client SDK: compute_hash() and upload_artifact() helpers
Build artifact-registry service API: POST /artifacts, GET /artifacts/{hash}, GET /artifacts?model_commit=...
Wire S3 storage with lifecycle rules and access controls
Add Console UI for artifact lineage and rollback action (read-only until RBAC approved)
Add runtime endpoint to fetch artifact by hash and perform safe swap with warm cache population

2026-02-28 Design feedback: UX wants explicit 'rollback preview' to show expected token-level latency/cost delta before swap (comment by Priya Rao).

2026-03-08 QA: initial validation harness re-running calibration on sample model produces 0.36% top-1 delta; within acceptance target.
2026-03-09 PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-registry/pull/112 — implements artifact API and storage adapter.
2026-03-10 Blocker: need S3 bucket policy updates for cross-account reads when Dedicated customers pin artifacts (security team ticket SEC-211)
testing_plan: Create synthetic calibration runs that are repeated 30x with same seed/tool_version to assert identical hashes
Run calibration with slight preprocessing noise to assert hash divergence and evaluate rollback safety
End-to-end integration test: upload artifact, perform console-triggered rollback in staging, run smoke test suite (latency, correctness)
Validation job: re-score 5 established prompts and compute statistical diff vs baseline; record in validation_report
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal-only registry (staging) and SDK release to inference team. Phase 2: Enable in Dedicated staging customers, add Console lineage view. Phase 3: GA with RBAC-controlled rollback and archived validation reports. Communicate breaking change: artifact canonicalization must be used by all calibration runs; deprecation window 60 days.
risks: Hash canonicalization is brittle — small numeric differences in calibration outputs can create different hashes even when accuracy is equivalent
Storage costs for full calibration blobs and validation reports could become significant
Rollback might produce unnoticed regressions if validation coverage is insufficient
Customer-managed private deployments may have inconsistent storage/registry availability; need adapter pattern
